hypothesis: Replacing the canonical single-file/shareable path with content-hashed external assets will make normal builds cacheable and deep-link safe while preserving P23 deployment limits and reducing initial transfer cost.

beforeEvidence.buildCommand: vite build --mode preview followed by frontend shareable generation

change: Made npm run build an ordinary application build with root-relative content-hashed CSS and JavaScript.
Applied the accepted P23 20,000,000-byte hero chunking limit to canonical, staging, and Production-mode builds.
Removed the active shareable/demo generators, outputs, tests, workflow references, and single-file plugin.
Removed unreachable Figma-export UI wrappers and dependencies after entry-graph proof.
Restored Apps Script as an independently generated and parity-checked recovery sidecar.
Added bounded stale dynamic-chunk recovery and fail-closed normal-asset deployment validation.

environment.deepLinkProbe: Vite preview /app/admin with exact dist/index.html hash and 200 CSS/JS responses

confounders: Artifact totals include 36,018,711 bytes of lazy hero media; those bytes are emitted for deployment but are not part of the initial route transfer.
A fresh Playwright browser journey was UNRUN because the pinned Chromium download timed out repeatedly in this workspace; deterministic unit gates and the real HTTP SPA fallback probe passed.

Wrangler dry-run passed after the U01 architecture and dependency retirement. A repeated invocation after the final two dead-wrapper deletions was policy-blocked before execution; the final staging artifact is smaller and independently passes manifest, marker, hero-identity, and per-asset budget checks.
rollback: Revert the isolated U01 commit. Do not restore generated shareable outputs by hand; Git history is the rollback/history location.
doNotRepeat: Do not reintroduce a single-file canonical build, tracked dist output, or dependencies reachable only from discarded export wrappers.
